q: 1. In stretching bond ..........
options: all the bricks are laid as headers
all the bricks are laid as stretchers
the arrangement of bricks is similar to English bond
the bonding bricks are laid at any angle other than zero or ninety degrees
explain: Stretching bond consists entirely of stretchers and is used primarily for half-brick thick partition walls.

q: 2. A type of bond in which all the bricks are laid as headers on the faces of walls, is known as ..........
explain: Heading bond uses only headers and is useful for constructing curved walls or footings.

q: 3. A bond consisting of heading and stretching courses so arranged that one heading course comes after several stretching courses, is called ..........
explain: Facing bond is used when expensive facing bricks are used for the outer skin and cheaper bricks for the backing.

q: 4. A stretcher bond is usually used for ..........
explain: Since all bricks are laid lengthwise, a stretcher bond cannot provide a transverse bond, limiting it to half-brick (10cm) walls.

q: 5. The most commonly used bond for all wall thickness is ..........
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond in brickwork and is the standard for most structural wall construction.

q: 6. Herring-bone bond is commonly used for ..........
explain: Herring-bone bond, where bricks are laid at 45 degrees, is highly decorative and provides excellent interlocking for floor pavings.

q: 7. In a raking bond ..........
options: the bricks are laid as headers
all the bricks are laid as stretchers
the arrangement of bricks is similar to English bond
the bonding bricks are laid at any angle other than zero or ninety degrees
explain: Raking bonds (like diagonal or herring-bone) involve laying bricks at an angle to increase longitudinal strength in thick walls.

q: 8. The arrangement of bricks is similar to English bond in ..........
explain: Dutch bond is a modified version of English bond that uses specialized patterns at the corners to avoid using too many closers.

q: 9. A wall built to resist the pressure of earth filling, is known as ..........
explain: A retaining wall is a structural wall designed to hold back soil or other materials at a slope steeper than the natural angle of repose.

q: 10. A retaining wall may be built in ...........
explain: Retaining walls are designed to resist lateral earth pressure and can be constructed using various materials like dry stone (gravity), masonry, or reinforced/plain concrete depending on height and site conditions.

q: 11. A retaining wall is commonly required in the construction of ..........
explain: Retaining walls are essential whenever there is a need to maintain a difference in ground surface elevation, common in hill roads, dam abutments, and bridge wing walls.

q: 12. A stone wall provided to protect the slopes of cutting in natural ground from the action of weather is known as ..........
explain: A breast wall is specifically designed to keep the natural ground slope in situ and protect it from weathering, unlike a retaining wall which usually supports backfill.

q: 13. The total horizontal pressure (p) per meter length of retaining wall at a depth h meter is ..........
explain: According to Rankine's theory, the total active earth pressure is P = 1/2 * w * h² * Ka, where Ka = (1-sinΦ)/(1+sinΦ).

q: 14. A partition wall may be ..........
explain: Partition walls are non-load bearing internal walls used to divide space; they can be permanent (fixed) or movable (folding/collapsible).

q: 15. Plain brick type of partition wall is constructed by ..........
options: laying bricks as stretchers in cement mortar
laying bricks as headers in cement mortar
reinforcing the brick wall with iron straps
brick work built within a frame-work of wooden members
explain: Plain brick partitions are typically half-brick thick (10 cm), achieved by laying bricks in the stretcher course.

q: 16. Brick noggin type of partition wall is constructed by ..........
options: laying bricks as stretchers in cement mortar
laying bricks as headers in cement mortar
reinforcing the brick wall with iron straps
brick work built within a frame-work of wooden members
explain: Brick nogging consists of a wooden framework (studs and noggins) filled with brickwork, used for stability and speed of construction.

q: 17. In a brick nogging type of partition wall, the vertical wooden members are called ..........
explain: In timber framing or brick nogging, the vertical members are called 'studs' while the horizontal members are 'noggings'.

q: 18. The sill in a wooden partition wall is the .......... wooden member.
explain: The sill is the lowest horizontal member of a frame that rests on the floor.

q: 19. In constructing concrete partition wall, the concrete mixture usually adopted is ..........
explain: M150 (approx. 1:2:4) is standard for non-structural or lightly loaded concrete partitions.

q: 20. The inner surface of an arch is called ..........
explain: The intrados is the lower or inner curve of an arch.

q: 21. The surface of the abutment on which the arch rests, is known as ..........
explain: The skewback is the inclined or splayed surface of an abutment prepared to receive the arch.

q: 22. The highest point on the extrados is called ..........
explain: The crown is the highest part of an arch, where the keystone is located.

q: 23. The vertical distance between the springing line and the highest point on the intrados is called .......... of the arch.
explain: Rise is the vertical distance from the level of the springing points to the highest point of the intrados.

q: 24. The wedge shaped unit (voussoir) placed at the crown of an arch, is called ..........
explain: The keystone is the central wedge-shaped stone at the summit of an arch, locking the whole together.

q: 25. The perpendicular distance between the intrados and extrados of an arch, is called ..........
explain: Depth or thickness of an arch is the distance between its inner (intrados) and outer (extrados) curves.

q: 26. The arch consisting of fully dressed stones, is called ..........
explain: Ashlar arches use finely dressed stones with thin joints for high-quality architectural work.

q: 27. In a flat arch, the skew back is made to rest in an inclined position so as to make an angle of .......... with the springing line.
explain: In flat arches, the skewback usually makes a 60-degree angle to provide sufficient lateral thrust for stability.

q: 28. The lower portion of an arch between the skew back and crown is called ..........
explain: The haunch is the lower half of the arch, between the crown and the skewback.

q: 29. The vertical distance between the wall plate and top of the ridge is called .......... of roof.
explain: Rise is the vertical distance from the horizontal plane of the eaves (wall plate) to the highest point of the ridge.

q: 30. In pitched roofs, the term gable is defined as the ..........
options: apex line of the sloping roof
inclination of the sides of a roof to the horizontal plane
horizontal distance between the internal faces of the walls
triangular upper part of a wall formed at the end of a pitch roof
explain: A gable is the triangular portion of a wall between the edges of intersecting roof pitches.

q: 31. The type of masonry in which the stones of the same height are used and the courses are also of the same height is called ..........
explain: In coursed rubble masonry, stones are roughly squared and laid in distinct horizontal layers (courses).

q: 32. The type of masonry in which the stones of irregular size and shapes are used and there are no regular course is called ..........
explain: Random rubble masonry is the most basic and cheapest form of stone walling, using stones as they come from the quarry.

q: 33. The type of masonry in which the stones are fine chisel dressed and the thickness of joints does not exceed 3 mm is called ..........
explain: Ashlar fine masonry uses perfectly squared, dressed stones with very thin mortar joints for a superior finish.

q: 34. When two blocks of stone have a tendency to be pulled apart in the direction of their lengths, then the type of joint used is called ..........
explain: A cramped joint uses a small metal 'cramp' (like a staple) to tie two stones together and resist tension.

q: 35. The wall constructed along the slopes to protect the slopes of cutting from the adverse effect of atmosphere are called as ..........
explain: Breast walls protect natural earth slopes from erosion and weathering, whereas retaining walls support man-made fills.

q: 36. The stretcher bond is generally used for ..........
explain: Stretcher bond is only suitable for walls that are half-brick thick (10 cm), like partition walls.

q: 37. Herringbone bond is used for ..........
options: architectural finish to the face work
walls having thickness more than 4 bricks
explain: Herringbone bond is a decorative pattern where bricks are laid at 45 degrees, common in flooring and very thick walls.

q: 38. To construct a 10 cm thick partition wall, preferred bond will be ..........
explain: A 10 cm wall is exactly the width of a single brick's length (stretcher side), hence stretcher bond is used.

q: 39. An external corner in brick masonry is called ..........
explain: The term quoin refers to the external corner of a wall or the stones/bricks used to form it.

q: 40. The part of a wall at the side of an opening in the masonry is called ..........
explain: Jambs are the vertical sides of an opening for a door or window.

q: 41. The nominal thickness of an expansion joints in brick wall must be more than ..........
explain: Expansion joints allow for thermal movement and are typically at least 20 mm wide.

q: 42. The operation finishing mortar joints after completion of a masonry wall is called ..........
explain: Pointing is the process of raking out mortar joints to a depth of 13-20 mm and refilling them with superior mortar.

q: 43. The most important tool used by a mason in laying of bricks while constructing a wall ..........
explain: The trowel is the primary tool for lifting and spreading mortar and for cutting bricks.

q: 44. Frogs made in the bricks are ..........
options: to reduce weight of the brick
to form a key for holding the mortar
to indicate year and name of the manufacture
to indicate top of the brick
explain: The frog is the indentation on the top face of the brick that creates a mechanical bond (key) with the mortar.

q: 45. In any case the bearing of a lintel should not be less than ..........
explain: Standard practice dictates a minimum bearing (overlap on the wall) of 15 cm or 1/10th to 1/12th of the span.

q: 46. For large spans the most suitable type of roof preferred is ..........
explain: Shell roofs are thin, curved R.C.C. structures that can cover very large spans without intermediate columns.

q: 47. In which of the following arch, the center the arch is above the springing line?
explain: A Horse-shoe arch (Moorish arch) has a curve that continues beyond the semi-circle, putting the center above the springing line.

q: 48. Which of the following scaffolding is provided for a building on the side of a busy street where the ordinary scaffolding will obstruct the traffic on road?
explain: Needle scaffolding (or cantilever scaffolding) is supported by 'needles' projecting through the wall, leaving the ground clear for traffic.

q: 49. Type of pointing in which V shaped projection is provided outside the wall surface is called ...........
explain: Toothed (or weathered) pointing involves creating a sloped or V-projection to help shed water from the joints.

q: 50. Broken bricks or stone chips are also called ...........
explain: Spalls are small chips or fragments of stone or brick, often used as filling material.
